newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says no word on US probe of passed secrets.
newsitem.headline: Israel says no word on US probe of passed secrets.

text.p: Israel said on Wednesday it had not been approached by U.S. authorities about reports that a Detroit engineer was suspected of divulging classified military information to the Jewish state over a 10-year period.

"Neither the Ministry of Defence nor any other Israeli authorities have thus far been approached by the U.S. authorities on the allegations reported today by the U.S. media," the Defence Ministry said in a statement.

The statement came after reports in the Detroit Free Press and Detroit News newspapers that the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) had searched the suburban Detroit home of David Tenenbaum, 39, on Friday on suspicions he had passed classified documents to Israel.
Tenenbaum, a mechanical engineer, worked for the Combat Vehicle Team at the U.S. Army Tank Automotive and Armaments Command in Warren, north of Detroit, the newspaper reports said.

According to court documents cited by the newspapers, he took an FBI polygraph last week as part of a background check for a higher security clearance. During the test, he said he inadvertently gave secret information to Israeli liaison officers assigned to the Warren facility, the reports said.
The U.S. Embassy in Israel said in a statement the matter came to the attention of the FBI last Thursday and that it had not been detremined whether any U.S. law had been broken.
"This matter is currently in the preliminary stages of an investigation. Importantly, no one has been arrested or charged with a crime," the embassy statement said.
The Israeli Defence Ministry said its personnel were under orders not to accept any secret U.S .information.

"All Ministry of Defence and Israeli Defence Forces officials in the USA are under the most explicit and categorical instructions to decline any and all offers of classified U.S. information," the ministry statement said.
The FBI was not immediately available for comment on the reports on Wednesday. Tenenbaum has not been charged with any crimes. No one one answered the telephone at his Southfield home on Wednesday.
FBI documents cited by the newspapers said the information allegedly passed by Tenenbaum related to countermeasures for the Patriot missile systems and test data for light-armour systems.

They said Tenenbaum could be charged with gathering and transmitting defence information, gathering and delivering information to aid a foreign government and disclosing classified information. Each of the federal charges carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $25,000 fine.
In their search FBI agents were looking for phone bills, bank and other financial statements, address books, computer files and documents relating to classified materials, the reports said.
